title: A screen reader user cannot move through the points on an exercise chart
what: On an exercise's progress chart, a past point can only be picked by touching and sliding a finger over the line. A screen reader user hears only the one number shown above the chart and cannot step to other dates or open the workout behind a point.
expected: Each point (or a step left / step right control) can be reached and read by a screen reader, and opening that point's workout works the same way.
who: members who use a screen reader
how_often: every time they open an exercise chart
fix_line: Make the chart a slider a screen reader can swipe through, saying each date and value, with open-workout on the picked point

title: On the month report calendar, the days trained are shown by colour only
what: The month calendar fills in the days trained with the orange colour. A screen reader reads each day as a plain number, so it cannot tell which days were trained, and someone who cannot see the colour well has only a slightly bolder number to go on.
expected: Each trained day says 'trained' to a screen reader, and has a mark besides colour (a tick or dot) on screen.
who: members who use a screen reader or see colour poorly
fix_line: Give each day a spoken name like '12, trained' and add a small mark to trained days

title: The minus 5 s, Stopwatch and plus 5 s buttons on the hold timer are small to tap
what: On the hold timer, the three buttons that set the countdown are 38 points tall with no extra touch room, below the app's own rule of at least 48 for every tap target. Mid-plank with sweaty hands they are easy to miss.
expected: Every button on the hold timer is at least 48 points to the finger, as the app's rule says.
how_often: every time they set a countdown
fix_line: Add extra touch room around these three buttons or make them 48 tall

title: The locked suggested-weight line can be tapped but looks like a grey note
what: For a free member, the line 'Suggested weight and reps: MettleUp Plus' under an exercise opens the MettleUp Plus explanation, but it is faint grey words with a small target icon and no arrow or lock, so it reads as a plain note.
expected: A line that opens something shows it can be tapped, for example with an arrow or a lock and a stronger colour.
who: free members once the Plus switch is on
fix_line: Add an arrow or lock to the line and give it the tappable colour

title: Tapping Not now a second time on a muscle tip stops it for good without saying so on screen
what: A muscle tip's Not now button always just says 'Not now'. The second time, it puts that tip away for good. Only a screen reader hears 'Don't suggest it again'; a sighted member is not told, and nothing on the card says where to get the tip back.
expected: The button's visible words change to say it will not ask again (as the spoken name already does), or the member is told where to turn the tip back on.
how_often: the second time they put off the same tip
fix_line: Show 'Not now, don't ask again' on the last Not now, matching the spoken words
